body: The issue here is floating point accuracy. You've set the axis lock of the body to only allow rotation around the Y axis and you've set the hinge axis to the Y axis. Axis lock always works in world space regardless of the body orientation. The hinge axis rotates along with the node transform. The HingeDoor2 node has been rotated a tiny amount around another axis than the Y axis. You cannot see this in the Inspector, but you can in the debugger: If you lock a body's rotation around 2 axis that are not perfectly aligned, you've fully constrained the rotation of the body, so the door cannot rotate anymore. This is what is happening here. I would suggest removing the angular lock from hinge_door.tscn. The reason why it works in godot physics is that it applies axis lock in a different way: it just resets the displacement of the locked axis. This causes energy to be lost, so is not correct.
